Package hadur2.core.duel

Class MoveDesign

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.duel.MoveDesign
final class MoveDesign extends Object
Duel-side switches for movement experiments; the move package never reads them.

    • GUN_SPLIT

      static final boolean GUN_SPLIT
      MOVE-15: movement by the enemy's gun (meant to be built with HEAT_WAVE). Once enough of the enemy's hits on us are of the learned class, the surf takes the protean pick at the hot setting on the held gun-heat wave; until then it takes the gun-heat wave afresh each tick (the stop-and-start), which does well against simple guns. When true it decides the hold and the protean switch; HEAT_HOLD and PROTEAN are then not read.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • REPLICATOR

      static final boolean REPLICATOR
      MOVE-16: the danger views' weights evolve by the replicator equation. Each enemy bullet that hits us multiplies a view's weight by how well it predicted the bullet's angle relative to the weighted average, with every view's share kept at 2% or more; off, the weights are fixed.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • GUN_GATE

      static final boolean GUN_GATE
      MOVE-17: the gun-heat wave (meant to be built with HEAT_WAVE and HEAT_HOLD false) is offered only while the enemy's gun is not a learning one by MOVE-15's count, so the stop-and-start is dropped against learning guns. Once the gun is called learning the surf is as with the gun-heat wave off. GUN_SPLIT, if on, wins: the gate is then not read.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • HOLD_650

      static final boolean HOLD_650
      DIST-3: no DIST-1 walk-in in a duel. The desired distance stays at the opening's (650 for a stranger) for the whole battle; END-1's finishing distance is unchanged.

    • STACK_LIST

      static final boolean STACK_LIST
      MOVE-23: the stop-and-start stack (MOVE-13 heatjit, SHIELD-14 swall, and MOVE-20, MOVE-21 and TIME-6 whenever those are on) applies only to opponents not on the stack off-list; a listed opponent plays as if those switches were off. The decision is made per opponent at run time; with this off the switches are the compile-time ones alone.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • RAM_HEAT

      static final boolean RAM_HEAT
      RAM-4: once the opponent is a confirmed rammer (RAM-2), the duel plays as with heatjit on (MOVE-11's gun-heat wave offered, MOVE-13's hold off) for the rest of the battle. The top-5 factorial put all of heatjit's gain on the rammers (+1.4 points) and a small loss on ranks 51-400, so this keeps the gain where it was measured. Off by default.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • RAM_BREAK

      static final boolean RAM_BREAK
      RAM-5: while RAM-2's escape drives, each path it weighs loses closest approach for every aim (head-on, linear) one of the rammer's shots in flight would hit it with. The 2026-10-28 rammer read (docs/bench/gap-to-2nd.md): against 12 nano rammers a linear aim would hit the escape on 52% of shots, Saguaro on 35%. Off by default.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FLATTENER_OFF

      static final boolean FLATTENER_OFF
      MOVE-24: in a duel the flattener views stay off (3.15). The top-5 factorial (PR #221) put flattener off at +0.12 +/- 0.10 APS on 1,212 bots, and the release-candidate census (PR #222) put it with swall at +0.34 +/- 0.15. Melee and team are untouched.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values
